content.text:
I wrote the solution to `benchmark/solution.ail`. When I ran it on `numbers.txt`, which holds 1 to 5, it printed `15`, matching the expected output exactly. It gives the same result whether the filename comes right after the source file or after `--`.

The program takes the filename from `getArgs()`, reads the file and splits it into lines. It then trims each line, turns it into a number with `stringToInt` and adds them up with `foldl`. Empty or non-numeric lines count as 0. If no filename is given, it prints a usage line instead.
